title: When Weights Collide with Latents: Direct Weight-Space Arithmetic Induces Asymmetric Degeneration in Sparse Autoencoder Monosemanticity
read_level: full text (19-page PDF via pdftotext); figures not inspected
metadata_mismatch: Concept DOI 24085180 resolves to version record 24085181. Paper subtitle 'A Comprehensive 30-Page Theoretical and Empirical Monograph...' but the PDF has 19 pages. Zenodo description advertises an 'Interactive Visualizer & Reproducible Colab Notebook', but the record contains only the PDF and no link appears in the paper. Metadata creator 'Mushfiqur Rahim, Md' matches.
why_wsp: Out of scope: studies how task-vector arithmetic (theta_base + lambda * tau, with tau from gradient fine-tuning) degrades SAE features; no editor reasons about weights, and the closed-form OLR-K fixes the SAE, not the model.
exclusion_reason: Task-vector arithmetic with gradient-fine-tuned vectors and SAE re-alignment; no LLM or reasoning editor authors the weights, and it is not positioned as a WSP baseline (WSP term used only via a citation that does not match the Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab 2026 source).
domain: mechanistic interpretability (sparse autoencoders) under task-vector weight edits
editor: none (task vectors from fine-tuning scaled by lambda; OLR-K is a Kabsch SVD rotation of the SAE dictionary)
target: unnamed '12-layer transformer' with top-k SAEs; replication claimed on GPT-2 Small (117M), Gemma-2-2B, LLaMA-3-8B

headline_results.claim: SAE reconstruction degrades with task-vector scale
headline_results.quote: scaling to λ = +1.0 inflates the MSE to 0.45034 (+67.9% error), and scaling to λ = +2.0 causes an explosion to 0.89832 (+235.0% error)
OLR-K reduces reconstruction MSE from 0.450 to 0.284, recovering 88.4% of baseline dictionary fidelity.
Across all three models, the asymmetry ratio remained bounded within ρ in [0.941, 0.962]

baselines_and_controls: Unperturbed model (lambda = 0); activation steering vs weight arithmetic (Table 5); SAE sparsity variants L1 / Top-K / JumpReLU (Table 3); dictionary expansion factors (Table 2).
runs_and_variance: "mean values computed over 2,048 evaluation sequences ... including 95% confidence intervals" (Table 1); number of seeds/models trained not reported
verification: proof sketches (Latent Orthogonality Drift, KV-Bypass, Frobenius lower bound); paired t-tests reported
limitations_stated: OLR-K recovery falls to 60% or below when |lambda| > 2.8; piecewise extension proposed (81.2% at lambda = 3.5).
cites_or_builds_on: 'Takehi, Y., Gu, A., & Andreas, J. (2024). Weight-Space Programming...' (MIT CSAIL Preprint, as cited; does not match the 2026 Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab blog)
notes_for_survey: Uses 'weight-space programming' as a synonym for task arithmetic and attributes it to a 2024 Takehi/Gu/Andreas preprint that does not match the known WSP source. No experimental details identify the base 12-layer model or task vectors. No statement on AI authorship in the record or paper.
